question: This run measured one plan card from an earlier question-tree run (../20261019-2344-tree/out/RESULT.md). The card asked whether feeding many GPUs to a block-tridiagonal Newton solve shortens its depth from T ordered steps to log2(T) (../20261019-2344-tree/out/RESULT.md). It proposed parallel cyclic reduction, which halves the system each round, against the Thomas algorithm, which walks the equations one after another. The card's own rule says lever only if the parallel solver beats one-thread Thomas by at least 2 times at 2^24 equations, and the speedup grows with size (QUESTION.md). An answer is the verdict of that rule, together with the numbers the card promised to measure later (RUN.md).
answer: By the card's own rule the answer is lever. At 2^24 equations the parallel solver took a median 21.8 ms against 7598.5 ms for one GPU thread running Thomas, a speedup of 348.3 (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The speedups at the five sizes were 8.54, 95.90, 517.53, 395.38 and 348.30, with a fitted slope of 0.256, so the growth test passed (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). Against one CPU core running the LAPACK routine through scipy, which took a median 416.7 ms at 2^24, the speedup was 19.1 (results_m2/out/records/id-E7_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). Both hand-written solvers first matched the vendor solver and scipy, with a largest relative residual of 3.11e-16 against a limit of 1e-10 (results_m2/out/records/id-E2_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json) (results_m2/out/records/id-E1_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json).
constraints: The problem is a chain of equations in which each equation links only its two neighbours, solved in double precision (QUESTION.md). The card fixed the hardware as one rented 40 GB data-centre GPU at 1.99 dollars an hour, and the run used that machine (RUN.md). The operator fixed its adjustments before any agent ran, among them no rewrite of the card, no optional phases, and a CPU floor that is reported but does not decide. The run had a hard cap of 8 dollars and at most two launches (RUN.md). The card had been rejected by its citation reviewer, and the run measured it anyway, as committed.
method: The runner generated tridiagonal systems from fixed seeds, with a diagonal of 3 and off-diagonals of plus or minus 1, at five sizes from 2^10 to 2^24 equations (QUESTION.md). Each size was timed on five seeds, and the speedup is the median Thomas time over the median parallel time (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). An anchor check at the two smallest sizes compared both hand-written solvers with the vendor solver on the GPU and with scipy on the CPU. The measurement code is one Python runner and one shell script that runs its stages in order on the box (run_m2.py) (onbox_m2.sh). The timed blocks repeat solves on data already on the GPU, so copies from the host are not in the times (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md). The baseline is one GPU thread per system, which the write-up calls the slowest sensible way to run Thomas (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md).
analysis: The operator sealed twelve predictions before any agent ran; ten held and two did not occur, for a Brier score of 0.090 (out/PREDICTIONS_SCORED.md). The forecast that the parallel solver would come within 3 times of the vendor solver failed, at 7.4 times slower (out/PREDICTIONS_SCORED.md). The measured speedup was 12.44 times the card's proxy of 28 (results_m2/out/records/id-E5_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The sweep took 0.119 hours against the planned need of 2 hours (results_m2/out/records/id-E10_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). Nothing was voided, and the optional phases were skipped by design. The box cost 0.48 dollars for 0.239 hours (RUN.md). A second run would time the copies to the GPU as well, and would read the result against the CPU library as the practical baseline.
